newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas up slightly in Q1, gas year in thin trad.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas up slightly in Q1, gas year in thin trad.

text.p: U.K. spot natural gas prices closed slightly stronger in the first quarter 1998 and in the gas year from October on Friday, traders and brokers said, although the market was generally quiet.

Winter prices softened, with trade done in Q1 98 at 16.85 pence a therm. But levels later recovered, and by the close Q1 was reported by a broker to be bid at 16.925 pence a therm against an offer at 17.00 pence.
"It's been all over the place," a dealer said. "The numbers keep changing hour by hour."
The gas year was also done at least twice at 13.00 pence a therm, after closing at 12.90/12.95 pence on Thursday, but most other periods were relatively quiet.
"Everyone's just sick of it at the moment," said a trader. "It's a very hard market to get anything done in."
While the OTC market was quiet, IPE futures saw another busy day with 255 lots done.
IPE prices were weaker in the winter but firmer next summer. The contract closed before the rally on OTC winter prices which brought spot winter prices back up late in the day.
